html:
The Propylaea is the great marble gateway to the Acropolis of Athens, built from 437 to 432 BCE. Its name means "that which stands before the gates".

It was the next big project of Pericles after the Parthenon, and its architect was Mnesicles. Visitors climbed a ramp and passed through a central hall with Doric columns outside and slender Ionic columns inside. A wing on the north side held paintings and may have served as a dining hall. On a bastion beside it stood the small Temple of Athena Nike.

The building was never finished. Work stopped in 432 BCE, as money and attention went to the coming Peloponnesian War, and some blocks still carry the rough knobs used to lift them into place. In later centuries it became part of a palace for the dukes of Athens, and the Ottomans kept gunpowder in it; an explosion in 1656 wrecked part of it. With the Parthenon and the Erechtheion it is one of the main buildings of the Acropolis today.
sum: The Propylaea is the great marble gateway to the Acropolis of Athens, built from 437 to 432 BCE. Its name means "that which stands before the gates".
